column1: # and what the downstream contract owes for it. Enforced by the SV-CONTRACT-CURRENCY doctrine
# ⛔ WHY IT EXISTS, measured not imagined: between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-19 the SV grammar shipped
# SEVEN semantically-distinct revisions while the contract kept saying `1.0.183`. The leaf that
# opened to fix that debt tracked the population BY HAND and its table went stale twice more inside
# the same week — `-0232` and `-0233` landed and were never added, so `-0237` was routed as "the
# FIFTH change" when it was the SEVENTH commit and the FIFTH to move a verdict. A hand-kept list of
# accept-set changes is the same object as the debt it tracks.
# semantic_digest = sha256 of the EBNF FRONTEND'S OWN `raw_ast` envelope — what the code generator
# consumes, from which comments are absent by construction. Re-derive:
# ⛔ To a FILE, never /dev/stdout — the tool writes progress there too and the JSON parse fails.
# commit: the revision's sha (8+ hex), or the word `PENDING` for the row of the commit being made —
#   and ONLY that row: tier A REFUSES a `PENDING` (or `(pending)`) row whose digest is already committed,
#   so the commit after a release back-fills the previous row first (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.23, 2026-09-24:
#   the test had read only `(pending)` against rows spelled `PENDING`, and 49 rows went unasked).
# ⛔ THE KEY IS THE DIGEST, NOT THE COMMIT. The first design keyed rows on the commit sha and had a
# chicken-and-egg the very next grammar change exposed: the row for the commit being made cannot
# carry that commit's own sha. The digest is known BEFORE the commit is, and it is the identity the
# contract actually describes, so `commit` is documentation and may be back-filled.
# disposition: RELEASE = the contract carries a section and the bug ledger carries a row.
#              NEUTRAL = comment-only; the digest EQUALS its predecessor's, which is what the
#              doctrine checks, so the claim refutes itself when false.
#              GENERATOR-ONLY = the digest MOVED and the generated PARSER did not. The revision
#              touches generation-side annotation text only (`@sample`), so the accept set and the
#              AST cannot have moved and no consumer of the parser can observe it. Ships no release,
#              owes no ledger row, and carries `parser_sha256=<64 hex>` in its notes; tier E hashes
#              generated/systemverilog_parser.rs and refuses on any difference.
#              ⛔ Added by SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.9 because a real change fit NEITHER existing slot: a
#              `@sample` repair moves the digest (annotations are in the raw_ast, comments are not),
#              so NEUTRAL refutes itself — while RELEASE would have bought its currency check with a
#              bug-ledger row describing a defect no released parser has. A vocabulary with a hole
#              in it does not fail loudly; it gets the nearest wrong label.
# ⛔ frontend_rekey: the digest is the FRONTEND'S reading of the grammar, so a frontend change re-keys every
# earlier row without a grammar byte moving. Each line below names the LAST commit whose rows were keyed by the
# reading before such a change; tier A does not re-derive commits at or before it (they are HISTORY, re-derivable
# only with the frontend of their day), and prints how many it skipped. EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION.6
# (2026-09-03): comments cut out of annotation payloads + `//` read as the meta-grammar's line comment.

SV-0069 (.13e.4) -- IEEE 1364-2005 puts NO signing on an integer or a time declaration: A.2.1.3 integer_declaration:152 and time_declaration:174 are `<kw> list_of_variable_identifiers ;`, A.2.8's block forms :314/:315 are the same, and neither `signing` nor `integer_atom_type` appears anywhere in that Annex. NARROW on verilog_2005 only. ⭐ THE GATE GOES ON THE OPTIONAL, NOT ON THE ALTERNATIVE: unlike SV-0068, the rule beside it (`integer_atom_type`) MUST stay reachable under verilog_2005 -- that admission is what makes plain `integer i;` parse -- so the .13e.5 _sv_only/_v2005 split is the wrong idiom here. One new rule `integer_atom_signing_sv_only := signing` @profiles [sv_2017, sv_2023], referenced inside the optional at both sites: no data_type alternative added, no branch index moved, `signing: $2` keeps its slot and is simply always absent under verilog_2005. ⛔ The routing evidence understated the defect TWICE and one command said so each time -- `time` is the same atom (integer_atom_type admits exactly integer + time under this profile) and `block_data_type:2077` is a second byte-identical site. Schema 26 unchanged (the sv_2017 typed AST is byte-identical across the edit, proven on 11 inputs by --interpret-parse-ast-json BEFORE any codegen).

The prose sha256 earlier in this row is left at 8bc4746aeb0363e9... deliberately: it records what the artifact hashed to when the row was written, which is history rather than a live claim.

SV-0071 (.13e.10(c4)) -- SIXTEEN IEEE-1800-only OPERATORS still reached the verilog_2005 profile, and the class was invisible to every census that preceded it: the .13e.7 instrument crosses profile-filtered reachability against IEEE 1364-2005 Annex B, a normative list of KEYWORDS, so a construct spelled entirely in PUNCTUATION can never become a candidate. The twelve compound assignments (`+= -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>= <<<= >>>=`, A.6.2 gives `=` and `<=` and nothing else) reach v2005 through `assignment_operator`; the three comparison/equivalence forms (`==? !=? <->`, A.8.6 defines none of them) through `binary_operator`; and `.*` (A.4.1 named_port_connection has no implicit form) through 7 hosts every one of which is NAMED `_sv_2017` while exactly THREE are @profiles-ADMITTED to verilog_2005 -- .13e.7's root cause verbatim, a naming convention is not an enforcement mechanism. Fixed with 16 whole-rule @profiles gates on the TERMINALS themselves, the SV-0031 `scope_resolution` idiom: gating the token root prunes the class in one place, where retagging the three mis-admitted hosts would not and would break legal Verilog.
